rubric.why: Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that heat is energy transferred, typically from a hotter body to a colder one.

rubric.why: Temperature indicates how hot or cold a body is.
rubric.description: Defines temperature as the degree of hotness or coldness.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that temperature measures the hotness or coldness of a body.

modelAnswer: Heat is energy transferred from a hotter body to a colder body because of a temperature difference.
Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.

items.followUp: Define the melting point and boiling point of a substance.

rubric.why: The lower fixed point is the ice point on the Celsius scale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the temperature of melting pure ice at standard atmospheric pressure, equal to 0°C.

rubric.why: The upper fixed point is the steam point on the Celsius scale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the temperature of steam above boiling pure water at standard atmospheric pressure, equal to 100°C.

modelAnswer: The lower fixed point is the temperature of melting pure ice at standard atmospheric pressure; it is 0°C on the Celsius scale.
The upper fixed point is the temperature of steam above boiling pure water at standard atmospheric pressure; it is 100°C on the Celsius scale.

items.followUp: Use a speed-time graph to derive the first equation of motion, v = u + at.

rubric.why: The displacement is obtained from the area under the speed-time graph.
rubric.description: Relates displacement to the area under the graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that displacement equals the area under the speed-time graph.

rubric.why: The rectangle under the graph has area ut.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the rectangular area as ut.

rubric.why: The triangular area is one-half base times height, with height v − u.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining the triangular area as 1/2 × t × (v − u).

rubric.why: Substituting v − u = at gives the second equation of motion.
rubric.description: Substitutes the acceleration relation and states the result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for reaching s = ut + 1/2at².

modelAnswer: Let the initial velocity be u, final velocity v, time t, acceleration a, and displacement s.
Displacement equals the area under the speed-time graph: s = area of rectangle + area of triangle.
Since v − u = at, s = ut + 1/2at².

items.followUp: A 0.20 kg stone moves in a circle of radius 2 m at 4 m s⁻¹. Find the tension in the string.

rubric.why: The mass and radius must be expressed in SI units and the speed identified.
rubric.description: States the given quantities in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for m = 0.1 kg, r = 1 m, and v = 5 m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: The string tension supplies the centripetal force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using T = mv²/r.

rubric.why: Correct substitution is needed to obtain the tension.
rubric.description: Substitutes the given values with units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for substituting the values into T = mv²/r.

rubric.why: The calculated tension is 2.5 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining 2.5.

rubric.why: Tension acts radially inward, toward the centre of the circle.
rubric.description: Gives the answer with unit and direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating T = 2.5 N and that it acts toward the centre.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 100 g = 0.1 kg, r = 1 m, v = 5 m s⁻¹.
Formula: T = mv²/r.
Substitution: T = (0.1 kg)(5 m s⁻¹)²/(1 m).
T = 2.5 kg m s⁻².
The tension is 2.5 N, directed toward the centre of the circle.

items.followUp: Define gravitational potential energy and derive its equation for an object raised through height h.

rubric.why: Kinetic energy is the energy an object possesses because of its motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking kinetic energy to the motion of an object.

rubric.why: Work done on the object is W = Fs, and the applied force is F = ma.
rubric.description: Sets up the work and force relations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using W = Fs and F = ma, or equivalent relations.

rubric.why: The work relation and equation of motion yield the change in kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for reaching W = 1/2m(v² − u²), or equivalent working leading to it.

rubric.why: For an object starting from rest, its kinetic energy is 1/2mv².
rubric.description: States the mathematical equation for kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final equation KE = 1/2mv².

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by an object due to its motion.
Work done on the object is W = Fs, and F = ma; therefore W = mas.
Using v² − u² = 2as, W = 1/2m(v² − u²).
For an object starting from rest, u = 0, so its kinetic energy is KE = 1/2mv².

items.followUp: A force has an x-component of 8 N and a y-component of 6 N. Find its magnitude and direction.

rubric.why: The perpendicular components combine using the Pythagorean theorem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using R = √(Fₓ² + Fᵧ²).

rubric.why: The resultant magnitude is 13 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining 13 N.

rubric.why: The direction angle follows from the ratio of the components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using tan θ = Fᵧ/Fₓ = 5/12.

rubric.why: The angle is approximately 22.6°.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining approximately 22.6°.

rubric.why: Both components are positive, so the vector is in the first quadrant.
rubric.description: States the direction relative to the axes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the force is 22.6° above the positive x-axis (or an equivalent first-quadrant direction).

modelAnswer: Given: Fₓ = 12 N and Fᵧ = 5 N.
Magnitude: R = √(Fₓ² + Fᵧ²) = √(12² + 5²) N = 13 N.
Direction: tan θ = Fᵧ/Fₓ = 5/12.
The force is 13 N at 22.6° above the positive x-axis.

items.followUp: What is a thermometric property? Give two examples used in thermometers.

rubric.why: A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it measures temperature.

rubric.why: A useful thermometric liquid should expand uniformly with temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for noting that the liquid expands uniformly or regularly.

rubric.why: The liquid should be visible in the thermometer tube.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for noting that the liquid is easily visible, often by being coloured.

rubric.why: The liquid should not stick to the glass and should remain liquid over a wide temperature range.
rubric.description: States a further useful property of the liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it does not wet/stick to glass or has suitable low freezing and high boiling points.

modelAnswer: A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature.
The liquid used in it should expand uniformly with temperature.
It should be easily visible in the narrow tube.
It should not wet or stick to the glass, and should have a low freezing point and a high boiling point.

items.followUp: A glass cube has side 4 cm and mass 150 g. If the density of glass is 2.5 g cm⁻³, find the volume of any cavity inside it.

rubric.why: The given values are correctly stated and, for the model solution, converted to SI units.
rubric.description: States the data and converts to SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for converting 5 cm to 0.05 m, 306 g to 0.306 kg, and 2.55 g cm⁻³ to 2550 kg m⁻³, or correctly using the original units.

rubric.why: The cube's external volume is its side cubed.
rubric.description: Calculates the external volume of the cube.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ m³ (or 125 cm³).

rubric.why: Density relates mass and volume of the glass material.
rubric.description: Uses the density relation to find the glass volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using Vglass = m/ρ.

rubric.why: The volume of glass material is obtained by dividing mass by density.
rubric.description: Substitutes the mass and density and calculates the glass volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining 1.2 × 10⁻⁴ m³ (or 120 cm³).

rubric.why: The cavity volume is the external cube volume minus the glass volume.
rubric.description: Finds and states the cavity volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for subtracting to obtain 5 × 10⁻⁶ m³, equivalent to 5 cm³.

modelAnswer: Given: side = 5 cm = 0.05 m, mass = 306 g = 0.306 kg, density = 2.55 g cm⁻³ = 2550 kg m⁻³.
Volume of cube = side³ = (0.05 m)³ = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ m³.
Volume of glass = mass/density = 0.306 kg/(2550 kg m⁻³) = 1.20 × 10⁻⁴ m³.
Volume of cavity = volume of cube − volume of glass.
Volume of cavity = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ − 1.20 × 10⁻⁴ = 5.0 × 10⁻⁶ m³ = 5 cm³.
